entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pietro Tagliavia d'Aragonia was an Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal who played a significant role in the Catholic Church during the Renaissance period. As Bishop of Vibo Valentia, he participated in several ecumenical councils, including the Council of Trent (1545-1563), which aimed to reform the Church and address issues related to its governance and doctrine. His involvement in these councils helped shape the Church's stance on various theological matters, such as the interpretation of Scripture and the role of indulgences.

A key figure in the Catholic Church during a time of significant religious and political upheaval, Pietro Tagliavia d'Aragonia's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime. His contributions to the Council of Trent had far-reaching consequences for the Church, influencing its stance on issues that would shape the course of Western history.

One lasting impact of Tagliavia d'Aragonia's work was the development of the Tridentine Mass, which became a central liturgical practice in the Catholic Church. This rite, established during the Council of Trent, remained in use for over 500 years and continues to influence Catholic worship practices today.
